newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson safe from Motorola fears.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson safe from Motorola fears.

text.p: Swedish telecom firm LM Ericsson should be insulated from some factors behind Motorola's third quarter profit warning, and analysts said on Thursday they were still positive towards the share.
"We have not changed our recommendations or forecasts regarding Ericsson because of this. Motorola's development differs from Ericsson's," said one analyst.
"The fact that Motorola warns about a price squeeze for semi-conductors is positive for Ericsson which is a net buyer of semi-conductors."
U.S. rival Motorola Inc on Wednesday announced that weak chip sales and competition in cellular phone sales would hurt its third quarter earnings and its share price fell three percent overnight.
"Ericsson buys components and if now Motorola signals lower prices the reactions should be positive," the analyst added.
Ericsson's half year report showed lower purchase costs which is partly an effect of the price squeeze on semi-conductors, another analyst said.
Motorola is losing market share within the mobile sector, which could also be positive for Ericsson, an analyst said.
"The most likely event is that Ericsson or Nokia has taken market share," said an analyst.
One reason for Motorola's falling market share is because it is changing its operations from an analogue system to digital, an analyst said.
"Both Motorola and Nokia are now readjusting to digital systems which is most likely one of the reasons for losing market share," said an analyst.
The share has recently risen strongly, and there is nothing, analysts said, which indicates that the share has reached its highest level even if temporary rebounds are possible.
"We are positive towards the sector, and even if temporary rebounds occur the share has not yet reached its all-time high," said an analyst.
The share has jumped 30 percent from its lowest level earlier this year.
"Motorola's profit warning rose because of the nervousness which could remain until Ericsson releases its next (third quarter) report in October," the analyst said.
Ericsson fell as much as 4.50 crowns after the Motorola news, but recovered somewhat before market close.
At 1030 GMT the share traded at 161 Swedish crowns, which was a rise of two crowns on the day.
